newsitem.title: FRANCE: French agency Publicis settles with True North.
newsitem.headline: French agency Publicis settles with True North.

text.p: French advertising agency Publicis SA said Thursday it settled a year-long dispute with its former U.S. ally, True North Communications Inc., parent of Foote, Cone & Belding (FCB), the largest U.S. advertising agency.
Publicis said it agreed to transfer agencies in Paris, London, Lisbon and Athens to FCB. Those offices were part of the Publicis FCB joint venture.

True North said it will form a new European network by uniting the four FCB offices it and Publicis formerly ran with Wilkens International, a 19-country pan-European advertising network bought by True North in January.
"We have got our own 100 percent-managed network in Europe, which we haven't had for the last 10 years," said Harry Reid, president of True North Communications International.
The accord gives Publicis ownership of the rest of the FCB European venture not transferred to True North. True North will transfer to Publicis "a portion" of its 49 percent stake in Publicis FCB.
The rest of the stake will be converted to give True North 26.5 percent of Publicis Communication, Publicis's advertising operating unit, up from 20.8 percent previously.
Publicis will maintain its 20 percent stake in True North and will be its largest shareholder.
The dispute between the two firms broke out publicly a year ago. But Reid said reports of infighting had been overdone.
The disagreement was prompted by a feeling on both sides that certain aspects of the agreement had been broken and "something had happened to the spirit of partnership," Reid said.

True North will also sell to Publicis its interest in the South African agency, The Partnership, and a majority interest in agencies either existing or to be spun-off from existing agencies in Argentina, Australia, New Zealand, India and Thailand.
